prerequisites: It is highly recommended that the student has passed the course Mechanics and Thermodynamics.
Students should have assimilated the basic knowledge of Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Mathematical Methods taught in the first year.
Specifically, students must master the concepts of thermometry and calorimetry, as well as the application of the first and second principles to closed systems and simple thermodynamic cycles.

learning_outcomes.text: Relate the scope of study of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer and know the most important applications of both disciplines in the field of Thermal Engineering.
Apply mass, energy, and entropy balances to various systems, including the main equipment present in industrial plants (engines, turbines, compressors, boilers, condensers, etc.).

Know the equipment that integrates power production cycles (steam, gas, and combined) and refrigeration cycles commonly used in industry, and be able to perform their thermodynamic analysis to assess their energy efficiency.
Know the main characteristics and fundamental physical laws on which the three basic mechanisms of heat transfer (conduction, convection, and radiation) are based.
Mathematically express the equations that describe heat transfer in a physical problem from fundamental balances (mass, momentum, and heat) and the laws on which the basic mechanisms are based.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I. APPLIED THERMODYNAMICS
Chapter 1. Properties and Processes in Thermodynamic Systems

Lesson 1: Basic concepts: Units of measurement. Gases: ideal, real and Van der Waals. Equations of state. Pure substance: phases and diagrams. State properties: determination using tables and/or equations of state.
Chapter 2. Basic Principles of Thermodynamics
Lesson 2. First Principle of Thermodynamics. Sign convention. Application to closed and open systems in steady state.
Lesson 3. Second Principle of Thermodynamics. Entropy definition and applications. Entropy generation. Isentropic efficiency of equipment.
Chapter 3. Thermal Machines
Lesson 4. The thermal machine: types and efficiency. The Carnot cycle: thermal efficiency. Cycles of thermal machines operating as engines: thermal efficiency.
Lesson 5. Gas power cycles: analysis of the Brayton cycle.
Lesson 6. Steam power cycles: analysis of the Rankine cycle. Combined cycle.
Lesson 7. Continuous refrigeration production by vapor compression of a refrigerant: analysis of the inverse Rankine cycle. The heat pump and its analysis.
BLOCK II. BASIC CONCEPTS OF HEAT TRANSFER
Chapter 4. Fundamentals of heat transfer
Lesson 8: Fundamental concepts, characteristics of basic heat transfer mechanisms and basic laws.
Chapter 5. Conduction
Lesson 9. Simple geometries: plane, cylindrical and spherical wall. Critical insulation radius.
Lesson 10. Additional surfaces: concept, temperature field, efficiency and dissipation coefficient. Heat transfer through finned surfaces.
Lesson 11. Heat transfer in common configurations: conduction shape factor.
Chapter 6. Convection
Lesson 12. Analysis methods in forced and natural convection.
Lesson 13. Use of empirical correlations in forced and natural convection.
Chapter 7. Radiation
Lesson 14. Fundamentals of thermal radiation. Radiative properties. Black body and gray body. Heat transfer by radiation between two surfaces. Combined heat transfer mechanisms.
teaching_methods: Virtual Campus activities (theoretical fundamentals, questionnaires, discussion forums, additional material)
assessment_rules: For students with continuous evaluation, the final grade is calculated as: NOTA = (0.1 x PA) + (0.1 x PL) + (0.1 x TG) + (0.7 x EX), provided the written exam (EX) score is 3.5 or higher. If EX is less than 3.5, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated formula result and 4.0. To pass the course, the final grade must be 5.0 or higher. For extraordinary exams, PA, PL, and TG scores from continuous evaluation are carried over. Students may opt to be examined on only one block (Block I or Block II) in the extraordinary exam, in which case the score from the last ordinary exam for the non-examined block will be computed if it was at least 3.5 points.
